scalesUsed.notes: A - B - C# - D - E - F# - G - A
scalesUsed.application: Governs the chord progression; the flattened 7th (G) provides the rebellious rock punch over the open A pedal note
The bedrock of Paul Kossoff's crying, expressive blues leads and biting unison bends
Blended into solo phrases for sweeter, vocal resolution to the chord tones of D and A

keyAndScale.keySignature: Three sharps (F#, C#, G#) for A major, but the persistent presence of G natural defines the Mixolydian tonal center
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: A major is relative to F# minor; A Mixolydian shares the key signature of D major (two sharps: F#, C#)

mainProgression.description: One of classic rock's most celebrated triad progressions. Triads of D major and G major are played over a continuous, ringing open 5th string (A) pedal tone, creating a huge sonic footprint with minimal finger movement.

sectionProgressions.progression: A - D/A - A - G/A - D/A - A
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: I - IV/I - I - bVII/I - IV/I - I
sectionProgressions.description: Staccato chord punches followed by generous, breathing space where the drums and rhythm lock tight
Guitar drops out almost entirely, leaving bass and hi-hat to drive the groove before stabbing syncopated accent chords
Full-throated rock cadence driving home the signature title hook with ringing open chords
Modulates into the relative minor (F#m) for melodic depth before resolving triumphantly back to A major

harmonicFunction: A (I) - Tonic chord anchoring the groove with authoritative open string power
D/A (IV/I) - Second-inversion subdominant chord that adds uplifting harmonic lift while retaining the low A root
G/A (bVII/I) - Subtonic triad introducing classic Mixolydian swagger without formal classical resolution
F#m (vi) - Relative minor providing soulful melancholy and dynamic contrast beneath the guitar solo
E (V) - Dominant major delivering the climactic turnaround tension leading back to the verse

techniques.name: Pedal-Tone Triad Inversions & Rhythmic Space
techniques.description: Playing upper-register D and G major triads on strings 4, 3, and 2 while letting the open 5th string (A) drone underneath, punctuated by strict rests that leave cavernous space for the rhythm section

notes: Hold down the A5 power chord with a single index finger barre at fret 2
Shift to D/A by placing middle finger on string 2 (fret 3) and ring finger on string 4 (fret 4)
Form G/A with fingers 1, 2, and 3 on frets 4, 3, and 5
Never pick string 6; keep it lightly dampened with the tip of the fret-hand index finger
Embrace the rests; the silence between chord stabs is just as powerful as the notes
sequence: Strike the A5 power chord firmly on beat 1
Snap the D/A chord on the 'and' of beat 2
Chop the sound immediately with pick-hand palm muting to produce crisp staccato
Deliver the G/A to D/A turnaround on the upbeat of beat 4
tips: Use a firm downstroke attack to ensure all strings speak with equal punch
Keep your wrist relaxed and resist the urge to fill the empty beats with strumming
Listen carefully to Simon Kirke's kick drum to synchronize chord chops
details.progression: A - D/A - A - G/A - D/A - A

techniques.name: Kossoff Soulful Vocal Hand Vibrato
techniques.description: Paul Kossoff's revered, wide, slow wrist vibrato executed by shaking the entire forearm and hand parallel to the neck, giving bent notes a human vocal cry with immense sustain

notes: Execute the whole-step bend to pitch before engaging vibrato
Anchor your thumb firmly over the top of the neck for leverage
Rotate the entire wrist and forearm as a single unit rather than wiggling the finger joint
Allow the note to blossom with natural tube amp compression and feedback
sequence: Bend the 7th fret G string (D) up a full step to E with fingers 3 and 2 supporting
Hold the peak pitch steady for a half beat
Initiate wide, circular forearm vibrato at approximately 4 cycles per second
Release smoothly back down into the root note
tips: Do not rush the vibrato; Kossoff's vibrato is slow, wide, and intensely emotional
A Les Paul bridge humbucker with a cranked Marshall power amp is the sonic blueprint
Use your fret-hand index finger to mute the surrounding lower strings to prevent sympathetic noise
details.progression: Solo over F#m - D - E progression

sections.name: Signature Space & Power Riff Intro
sections.description: One of the most famous rock entrances in history. Crisp, biting Marshall chord stabs explode out of total silence, alternating between A5, D/A, and G/A.
sections.progression: A - D/A - A - G/A - D/A - A
notes: Hit the A chord on beat 1 and immediately mute on beat 2
Let the open A string ring as the pedal tone throughout all triad changes
Chop the chords staccato to keep the rhythm crisp and explosive
Keep low E string silent with index finger muting

sections.name: Verse Minimalist Groove & Bass Space
sections.description: Paul Kossoff drops out of the arrangement, leaving Andy Fraser's melodic bassline and Paul Rodgers' vocals to command the spotlight before stabbing isolated chord accents.
notes: Resist the temptation to strum continuously; silence creates the groove
Enter with decisive, ringing chord punches at section markers
Keep your guitar volume knob ready to roll back for clean dynamics
Lock eyes with the snare hit when executing accent chords

sections.name: Pre-Chorus Rising Tension
sections.description: Harmonic energy escalates as the guitar re-enters with driving syncopated downstrokes, propelling the arrangement into the stadium chorus.
notes: Play full open G and D major chords to expand the harmonic width
Dig into the pick attack as the vocal phrasing intensifies
Accent the downbeat transitions into each chord change
Let the open strings ring with natural sustain

sections.name: Chorus Anthem Hook
sections.description: The quintessential sing-along hook. Kossoff blends the driving intro triad riff with full-throated power chords, driving the title phrase home.
notes: Coordinate chord stabs with the vocal phrasing 'All right now'
Use open A string pedal tone to glue the progression together
Apply aggressive right-hand downstrokes for maximum punch
Allow the final A chord to ring out over the vocal sustain

sections.name: Paul Kossoff Iconic Melodic Solo
sections.description: One of classic rock's most studied and expressive guitar solos. Kossoff proves that note selection, space, and crying vocal vibrato trump blazing speed every time.
notes: Begin with the famous double-stop bend on strings 2 and 3 at the 14th fret
Hit target chord tones squarely on the downbeat of chord transitions
Apply wide, slow forearm vibrato to every sustained note
Let the amplifier power tubes breathe with natural overdriven warmth

sections.name: Outro Riff Vamp & Climax
sections.description: The band locks into an unyielding groove. Kossoff weaves energetic blues fills and double stops between the driving A-D/A-G/A chord framework.
sections.progression: A - D/A - A - G/A - D/A - A
notes: Vary the intensity of the chord chops as the jam builds energy
Drop subtle blues licks into the silent gaps between chord stabs
Maintain unwavering tempo discipline through the extended vamp
End on a resolute, sustained A5 chord ringout

guitar.recommended: 1959 Gibson Les Paul Standard 'Burst' with PAF humbuckers
guitar.pickup: Bridge humbucker with tone on 10 and volume on 9 for responsive touch sensitivity

amp.recommended: Marshall 1959 Super Lead 100W through Marshall 4x12 basketweave cabinet with Celestion Greenbacks

effects.distortion: Pure power-tube saturation from cranked British tube amplifier
effects.reverb: Subtle studio plate reverb to replicate the Olympic Studios live room sound
effects.other: No pedals; direct guitar-into-amp connection for maximum touch response

beginner.title: Mastering the Open A Pedal Chords
steps: Learn the fingering for A5, D/A, and G/A while keeping the 5th string open
Practice muting the low 6th string with the fret-hand index finger pad
Work on stopping the chords cleanly with palm muting at 80 BPM
beginner.goals: Play the signature intro riff with accurate chord fingerings and clean string muting

intermediate.title: Groove, Timing & Rhythmic Space
steps: Count the rests strictly to avoid rushing the silent gaps in the verse and intro
Synchronize your downstroke stabs with a metronome at full 120 BPM tempo
Play through the verse, pre-chorus, and chorus transitions smoothly
intermediate.goals: Perform the complete rhythm guitar track in the pocket with confident dynamic restraint

advanced.title: The Kossoff Vibrato & Solo Nuances
steps: Develop the forearm rotation technique for wide, slow, vocal vibrato
Transcribe and perform the expressive bends and microtonal inflections in the solo
Improvise blues-rock phrases in F# minor and A major with intentional note placement
advanced.goals: Execute Paul Kossoff's solo with authentic tone, pitch precision, and deep emotional vibrato

similarTechniques.title: You Shook Me All Night Long

commonMistakes: Letting the low E string ring out, creating a muddy dissonant low end beneath the A pedal chords
Strumming through the rests rather than embracing the silence that defines the song's swagger
Using a fast, nervous finger vibrato instead of Kossoff's wide, slow, singing forearm movement
Over-saturating the amplifier with modern high-gain distortion, which destroys the punch of the chord attacks
practiceRoutine: 5 mins: A5, D/A, G/A chord transition drills with thumb and index muting check
10 mins: Slow metronome practice at 90 BPM counting '1 and 2 and 3 and 4 and' to master the rests
10 mins: Kossoff vibrato drills on whole-step bends at frets 7, 9, and 14
10 mins: Solo phrase phrasing and dynamic control against a backing track
focusAreas: Total silence during rests through simultaneous pick-hand and fret-hand muting
Clean pick attack across strings 5, 4, 3, and 2 without touching string 6
Slow, circular wrist/forearm vibrato on sustained lead notes
metronomeWork: Practice the intro riff with the metronome clicking on all four quarter notes at 85 BPM
Shift the metronome to click exclusively on beats 2 and 4 to internalize the classic rock backbeat
Increase tempo gradually up to the album's native 120 BPM pocket
